api: A remote MCP endpoint at https://mcp.portablecontext.ai/mcp over streamable HTTP, authenticated with OAuth 2.0 and PKCE. No API key is issued; sign-in happens on first connect. A web dashboard at app.portablecontext.ai manages containers and connections.
cons: Early access at v0.4, with signup released in controlled batches
Free but capped during early access, and the terms reserve the right to introduce a price with notice, so long-run cost is unknown
Operated by an individual rather than a disclosed company, which is a continuity risk no policy text resolves
The repository is a source snapshot, not a runnable self-hosted distribution, so the open licence does not currently deliver an exit
Only works with clients that support custom MCP connections
name: PCD (Portable Context Deck)
pros: One endpoint serves every MCP-capable client, so context is not locked to a single assistant
Export to JSON and Markdown means the deck is not trapped in the service
Public core is published under AGPL-3.0, so the mechanism is inspectable
files: Containers the vendor calls preferences, traits, skills, work, knowledge, history, specialists and connections. The knowledge container is described as queryable and scoped to the deck. Changes are versioned and committed, and decks export to JSON and Markdown.
value: Keeps the context you would otherwise re-explain at the start of every AI session in one deck, reachable over a single Model Context Protocol endpoint. A client connects, loads the deck, and starts with your preferences, standing guidelines, saved procedures, live work state and knowledge base already in place. The point is portability: the same deck is available in whichever assistant, IDE or chat client you are working in that day.
engine: None of its own. PCD carries context to whichever model the connected client is running; it is a context layer, not a model.

pricing.limits: Capped usage; signup released in controlled batches
pricing.includes: Full product setup: MCP endpoint, dashboard, connection management, and export

tagline: A portable context layer that loads your preferences, work state and knowledge into any MCP-capable AI client.
use_cases: Carrying one working context across several AI clients rather than re-briefing each
Resuming a project days later without re-establishing what was in progress
Giving domain-scoped specialists a shared base of context and skills
integrations: Any client supporting custom Model Context Protocol connections
Client-connected connectors reached through the deck
governance_note: A portable context layer concentrates in one place the material a person would otherwise spread across separate assistants: standing instructions, work in progress, and an accumulated knowledge base. That concentration is the product, and it is also the risk, because a single credential then reaches all of it. The published terms and privacy policy answer more of the usual questions than most services at this stage. PCD is operated by Andrea Dellanoce in Belgium, named as the data controller, with Belgian law applying and the Belgian Data Protection Authority named as the supervisory route for complaints. The privacy policy lists its processors, Cloudflare, Supabase, Resend, and Sampark Inc trading as Composio, with transfer bases stated, and gives server-log retention as seven days. The policy states that private context is not sold and not used to train or fine-tune a model, and decks export to JSON and Markdown. The minimum age is 16. What remains open is the shape of the operator: a service run by a named individual rather than an incorporated entity carries continuity risk that no policy text addresses, so the export path is the control that matters most here.
training_optout: The privacy policy states that private context is not sold and is not used to train or fine-tune a model. Processors are listed with transfer bases, and server logs are kept for seven days.
